Background reading and **reference material** the workshop's chapters cite into — single-cell biology, statistics, shell scripting, Git, databases, file formats, and a methods-section template. Read what you need, when you need it.

These materials support the core workshop but are not part of the three-day sequence — they're linked from **[Additional Resources](../Additional_Resources.html)**. Quick one-page references (R, Seurat, ggplot2, SLURM, Git…) are on the separate **[Cheat Sheets](../Cheat_Sheets.html)** tab.

::: callout-note
**Getting up and running (R, the command line, computers & HPC).** That material is now the two **Day 0 modules** — work them before the workshop if any of it is rusty:

- [P1 — Computer Systems & the Command Line](Chapter_P1_Computer_Systems.html) — how computers and operating systems work, using VS Code on your own laptop, and the command line (navigation, paths, pipes). (The Talapas cluster track — VS Code Remote-SSH, Lmod, SLURM, and reproducible environments — is [Module 09](Chapter_09_SLURM_Basics.html) on Friday.)
- [P2 — R & RStudio](Chapter_P2_R_and_CommandLine.html) — R, RStudio, data structures, functions, the tidyverse, reading/writing data.
:::

## Appendices — reference material

Listed in the order they tend to come up across the workshop flow.

| # | Appendix | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| A | [Single-Cell Biology Refresher](Appendix_A_SC_Biology_Refresher.html) | The molecular biology behind scRNA-seq — read this before Lecture 00 if your bio is rusty |
| B | [Statistical Foundations](Appendix_B_Statistical_Foundations.html) | NB / Poisson, design matrices, FDR, shrinkage, why per-cell tests fail |
| C | [GREP, Regular Expressions & Shell Scripting](Appendix_C_GREP_Regex_Shell.html) | Pattern matching with `grep`, regex syntax, writing reusable shell scripts |
| D | [Git, GitHub & Version Control](Appendix_D_Git_GitHub.html) | Tracking changes with Git, collaborating on GitHub, common workflows |
| E | [Gene-Expression Databases & File Formats](Appendix_E_Databases_FileFormats.html) | The big-six scRNA-seq repositories and a field guide to every file format |
| F | [Common Bioinformatics File Formats](Appendix_F_Bioinformatics_File_Formats.html) | A field guide to FASTA, FASTQ, SAM/BAM, GFF3/GTF, BED, VCF, BigWIG, and the single-cell containers — with annotated head-of-file examples |
| G | [Methods-Section Template](Appendix_G_Methods_Template.html) | Annotated boilerplate for an scRNA-seq paper's methods section |
| H | [Core R Commands Reference](Appendix_H_Core_R_Commands.html) | A task-organised look-up for the R you use in every tutorial — vectors, data frames, dplyr, ggplot2, reading/writing data |
| I | [Quarto & Markdown Syntax](Appendix_I_Quarto_Markdown.html) | The markup behind every page here — headings, code chunks & options, figures, callouts, tabsets, math, and citations |

The **[Glossary](Glossary.html)** of single-cell terminology is at the top of the [Additional Resources](../Additional_Resources.html) page; read it alongside the lectures.

## How to use these resources

::: callout-tip
**Read on demand.** The workshop [chapters](../Materials.html) cross-reference these liberally — when a chapter says "see Appendix B § 8 for why per-cell DE fails", that's a hint to read that section before continuing.

**If you're new to the toolchain:** start with the two [Day 0 modules](../Materials.html) (R, the command line, computers & HPC) before Day 1.

**If your molecular biology is rusty:** Appendix A, before Lecture 00.

**If your statistics is rusty:** Appendix B, before Lecture 05 / Chapter 5.

**Once you start writing up your own scRNA-seq results:** keep Appendix G (Methods-Section Template) open in another tab.
:::
